name: Vonda Velour

inspiration.original: Max Renn and the Videodrome signal
inspiration.oldScript: The tape that rewires its viewer was body horror told through a man's gaze at women's bodies on a screen.
inspiration.newLens: An aerobics queen whose real voice was dubbed over by her producer. The monster is the diet-culture voice that calls every body a 'before'.

logline: Pop in the tape and your feet start moving. They don't stop. Vonda Velour wants you to burn it off, all of it, until there's nothing left of you to burn.
backstory: Wanda Fenn was the best dancer the Glitter Box ever had: big laugh, big hips, a split on any beat, and a Thursday class she called Dance for Every Body. In 1983 a video producer named Rex Brannigan saw her teach and offered her a starring role. Then he renamed her Vonda Velour, ordered her to lose thirty pounds before the shoot, and weighed her every morning at Pump Iron Gym in front of the crew. When she refused to say the lines he wrote, he hired another woman to dub them in. The tape, BURN IT OFF! with Vonda Velour, sold a million copies, and every one of them said things Wanda never said: every bite is a betrayal, nobody loves a before picture, no pain, no gain. Wanda quit, moved to Sacramento and never danced on camera again. Brannigan went bankrupt in 1985. But the tape kept playing in living rooms and gym classes, and this October the Heartstone woke it up. Now the Vonda on the screen steps out of it, a glossy, glittering, smiling thing in a magenta leotard made of Brannigan's script and every cruel thing anyone ever said about a body. Anyone who watches works out until they drop, and her followers, the Burners, jog the streets before dawn in magenta sweatbands, chanting.

centralIssue.title: The voice that says your body is a problem
centralIssue.summary: Vonda Velour never said most of what's on that tape. A producer starved a joyful dancer, dubbed his own cruelty into her mouth and sold it to a million living rooms. The voice the Burners obey is diet culture in leg warmers. Find Wanda's real words and let the town move for joy instead of punishment.

poster: A glittering aerobics queen in a magenta leotard, teal leg warmers and a headset microphone bursting out of a giant television screen, her smile impossibly wide, an army of exhausted joggers in matching sweatbands running in rings around a glowing purple geode on a suburban street below
portrait: Close portrait of a glossy 1980s aerobics star with enormous teased blond hair, a magenta sweatband, frosted pink lipstick and a headset microphone, her smile frozen and too bright, faint VHS tracking lines rippling across her face
endingPhoto: A glittering aerobics queen in a magenta leotard, teal leg warmers and a headset microphone climbing halfway out of a giant curved television screen in a dark living room, one hand reaching for the remote, static crackling off her teeth, exhausted joggers in sweatbands collapsing across the shag carpet behind her mid-jumping-jack
taunts: And burn, two, three, four! Burn that lunch right off!
Feel that? That's weakness leaving your body, sweetie!
Again! Again! No pain, no gain!

clues.title: The shooting schedule
clues.hint: BURN IT OFF! was filmed in Studio A at Pump Iron Gym in 1983. Sunny Castellanos teaches in the same room now.

encounter.title: Studio A, Mirror Wall
encounter.place: Studio A, Pump Iron Gym and Aerobics
encounter.text: Studio A still has the gold-flecked mirror wall from the video. Sunny is setting up for her Wheels and Heels class, rolling between stacks of step boxes. Taped to the mirror, curled and yellow, is a 1983 call sheet: BRANNIGAN HOME VIDEO. BURN IT OFF! DAY 3. TALENT TO WEIGH IN AT 6 A.M. When you glance at your reflection, it's doing jumping jacks. You aren't.
encounter.art: A gym aerobics studio in afternoon sun with a gold-flecked mirror wall, a 22-year-old Puerto Rican woman with a mane of dark curls, an orange terry headband and a teal leotard rolling her neon-orange racing wheelchair between stacks of step boxes, a curled yellow sheet of paper taped to the mirror, a teenager standing still while their reflection in the mirror does jumping jacks, bright window light, medium wide shot

choices.label: Ask Sunny what she remembers about the shoot

success.text: Sunny was nineteen and an extra in the back row. "Wanda. That was her real name. Best dancer I ever saw. Brannigan put a scale in the middle of this floor and weighed her every morning in front of everybody. By day five she couldn't climb the stairs." Sunny's jaw sets. "That tape is his. It was never hers."
success.art: A young woman in a wheelchair speaking with fierce emotion in an aerobics studio, pointing at a spot on the floor where a scale once stood, a teenager listening

failure.text: Sunny's class starts and the music is too loud to talk over. Your reflection keeps going, faster and faster, and you realize your own knees have started bouncing in time. It takes two full minutes to make them stop.
failure.art: A teenager struggling to hold still in a packed aerobics class while their reflection in the mirror wall bounces frantically, knees already starting to bob

choices.label: Peel the call sheet off the mirror and read the back

success.text: On the back, in looping purple ink, someone wrote notes to herself: Day 5. He changed my lines again. I said, dance because it feels good. He wants, every bite is a betrayal. I won't say it. He says fine, he'll dub it. Signed with a little heart: W.F.
success.art: The back of a yellowed call sheet covered in looping purple handwriting, a small drawn heart beside the initials, a teenager holding it up to the studio light

failure.text: The paper tears in half. The mirror wall ripples like water, and a hundred reflections of a woman in a magenta leotard lean forward through the glass and chant, "Weigh in. Weigh in. Weigh in."
failure.art: A rippling mirror wall with dozens of reflections of a glossy aerobics star leaning out and chanting, a teenager clutching a torn paper and backing away

clues.title: The raw footage
clues.hint: Zelda at Rewind Video says every movie has a version the studio didn't want anyone to see.

encounter.title: Bankruptcy Auction, Box 14
encounter.text: The back room of Rewind Video is a canyon of returns, bootlegs and dead VCRs. Zelda leans on a box stenciled BRANNIGAN HOME VIDEO, BANKRUPTCY AUCTION 1985. Inside: forty shrink-wrapped copies of BURN IT OFF! and one unlabeled tape in a padded case. On the shelf above, every copy of BURN IT OFF! in the store is humming a count of eight under its breath.
encounter.art: The cramped back room of a 1980s video rental store piled with videotapes and dead video decks, a 63-year-old woman with a silver-streaked black bouffant, cat-eye glasses on a pearl chain, red lipstick and a red staff vest leaning on an open stenciled cardboard box of shrink-wrapped tapes, a shelf above lined with pink aerobics tapes glowing faintly, a teenager holding one unmarked tape in a padded case, a single hanging bulb, medium shot

choices.label: Ask Zelda what she knows about Rex Brannigan

success.text: Zelda snorts. "Rex Brannigan. Produced two of my pictures in '57 and docked my pay for every pound I gained." She hands you the unlabeled tape. "The raw footage. Before he got his scissors on it." On the store monitor, a radiant, round, sweaty woman grins straight into the lens: "Your body isn't a before picture, baby. It's the whole movie."
success.art: A small video store monitor showing a joyful, sweaty, curvy dancer in a leotard laughing into the camera, a teenager and an older woman watching side by side in the dim back room

failure.text: Zelda gets pulled away by a man arguing about late fees. When you reach for the box, every monitor in the store clicks on at once, and Vonda points straight out of the screen at you: "You! In the back! Burn it!"
failure.art: A wall of video store monitors all showing the same glossy aerobics star pointing directly out of the screen, a teenager frozen beside a cardboard box

choices.label: Rig two VCRs and dub the raw tape before anyone notices

success.text: Two VCRs, one patch cable, a lot of jiggling. The raw footage plays as it copies: take after take of Wanda laughing, flubbing, dancing off the count for the pure fun of it. Once she looks straight down the lens and says, "If anybody ever tells you to burn yourself up, you tell them Wanda said no."
success.art: Two stacked VCRs connected by a patch cable in a messy back room, a monitor showing a laughing dancer, a teenager's hands pressing record

failure.text: The tape heads chew the raw reel and spit it out crinkled. The copy you made is only the dubbed version, and it keeps playing on the monitor even after you yank the plug.
failure.art: A crinkled ribbon of videotape spilling out of a VCR, an unplugged monitor still glowing with an aerobics star mid-kick

clues.title: The index cards
clues.hint: Coach Pruitt refuses to play BURN IT OFF! in gym class, and the school district has noticed.

encounter.title: Coach Pruitt's Office
encounter.place: The PE office, Glimmer Falls High
encounter.text: Coach Tammy Jo Pruitt's office is softballs, dented trophies and a framed photo of her own 1958 high-school state-champion team. On her desk lies a district memo stamped MANDATORY: all PE classes will perform BURN IT OFF! daily and record student weights weekly. Under it is a stack of index cards, each in a different kid's handwriting. Coach is on the phone with the superintendent and losing her patience at a volume you can hear from the parking lot.
encounter.art: A cluttered high school PE office, softballs in a bucket, dented trophies on shelves, a framed black-and-white photo of a 1958 girls' softball team, a tall broad woman in her forties with a sunburned freckled face, a red-blonde perm under a green ball cap and a green and gold windbreaker shouting into a desk phone, a stamped memo and a stack of small white index slips on the desk, a teenager waiting in the doorway, fluorescent light, medium shot

choices.label: Wait out the phone call and ask her straight

success.text: Coach slams down the phone. "I will not weigh children. Not in my gym." She slides you the cards: anonymous notes kids left in the counselor's box after doing the tape at home. Skipping lunch. Dizzy in class. Hearing Vonda's voice every time they eat. "Same voice, every kid," she says. "That's not some lady on a tape. That's every grown-up who ever told a kid her body was wrong."
success.art: A fierce gray-haired coach leaning across her desk to hand a stack of index cards to a teenager, a crumpled district memo in the trash can beside her

failure.text: Coach is too deep in the fight to talk and points you at the door. In the hallway the PA crackles, a perky voice counts to eight, and the whole lunch line starts doing silent step-touches.
failure.art: A school hallway where a line of students with lunch trays all step-touch in eerie unison beneath a crackling PA speaker, a teenager staring

choices.label: Read the index cards while she's yelling

success.text: I did the tape three times today. Vonda says I'm a before picture. I don't eat lunch anymore because she's watching. At the bottom of the stack is one older card in purple ink, postmarked Sacramento, 1984: To any kid using my tape, I'm so sorry. Those weren't my words. Love your body. Dance because it feels good. Wanda.
success.art: A spread of handwritten index cards on a desk, one older card in purple ink with a Sacramento postmark standing out among them

failure.text: Coach catches you mid-card. "Those are private." She's right, and the look she gives you is worse than detention. The cards go into a locked drawer, and the guilt goes home with you.
failure.art: A coach with a phone still to her ear placing a firm hand over a stack of index cards, a guilty teenager looking at the floor

signature.title: Rewind and Repeat
signature.text: The TV turns itself on. The VCR swallows a tape you didn't put in. Synth drums, a gold-flecked studio, and Vonda Velour in a magenta leotard and teal leg warmers with a smile as wide as the screen: "Good morning, Burners! Let's burn off everything you ate today!" Your feet start moving. You can't make them stop.
signature.art: A dark suburban living room at one in the morning lit by a glowing console television, on screen a glossy aerobics star with enormous teased blond hair, a magenta sweatband, a magenta leotard, teal leg warmers and a headset microphone kicking high in a gold-flecked studio, a video deck on the shelf below with its tape slot lit, a teenager in pajamas on the shag carpet doing jumping jacks with a panicked face, magenta TV glow, medium wide shot

choices.label: Drag yourself to the wall and yank the plug

success.text: Your legs keep grapevining toward the TV, so you drop and crawl on your elbows. The plug comes out with a pop and a fat blue spark. Static. You lie on the carpet laughing and panting and refusing to move a single muscle for an hour.
success.art: A teenager sprawled on shag carpet triumphantly holding a yanked power plug, the television screen collapsing to a dot of static

failure.text: The TV keeps playing without the plug. Vonda leans halfway out of the screen. "Quitters don't get results!" You dance until four in the morning and wake up with legs like wet noodles.
failure.art: An aerobics star leaning out of an unplugged television toward an exhausted teenager still dancing, the cord dangling uselessly

choices.label: Dance it wrong on purpose: off-beat, silly, joyful

success.text: You do the Sprinkler. The Robot. A disco point so bad it's art. Vonda's count stumbles. "And burn, and, and..." She can't sync to someone having fun. The tape stretches like taffy, and the VCR spits it out onto the carpet.
success.art: A teenager doing a goofy disco pose in lucky leg warmers in front of a television showing a glitching, confused aerobics star, a videotape ejecting from the VCR

failure.text: You try, but your body snaps back into her count like a rubber band. "Cute," says Vonda. "Now do it right." You do a hundred jumping jacks. Somewhere upstairs, so do your parents.
failure.art: A teenager doing rigid jumping jacks in front of a smirking aerobics star on TV, shadows of parents doing the same on the upstairs landing

signature.title: The Burners
signature.text: Before dawn a column of joggers comes up Crystal Street in matching magenta sweatbands: your neighbors, your science teacher, the mailman, all in perfect step with glassy eyes, chanting, "No pain, no gain, no pain, no gain." At the front, Mrs. Haskins from down the street carries a boombox like a holy relic. Some of them are limping. None of them stop. One of them is a kid from your homeroom.
signature.art: A suburban street at four in the morning before dawn, a column of neighbors jogging in perfect step in matching magenta sweatbands with glassy eyes, a schoolteacher, a mailman in uniform and a middle-aged woman at the front holding a boombox high over her head, a young teen in the column limping, a teenager on the curb holding a bag of rock salt, blue predawn light and orange streetlights, wide shot from the sidewalk

choices.label: Pour a line of rock salt across the street

success.text: The column hits the line and stumbles. Sweatbands slip. A dozen people blink like they've just woken up in the street in their running shorts. The kid from your homeroom sits down hard on the curb and asks for a glass of water.
success.art: Joggers stumbling over a glittering white line of rock salt across asphalt, sweatbands slipping off, a young teen sitting dazed on the curb

failure.text: They jog right over it, crunching, chanting louder, and somehow you are in the column too, running and chanting, until the sun comes up and you fold onto somebody's lawn like a lawn chair.
failure.art: A teenager jogging glassy-eyed inside a column of sweatbanded runners at sunrise, a scattered line of rock salt crushed underfoot behind them

choices.label: Grab the kid from homeroom out of the column

success.text: You hook their arm and haul them onto a lawn. They fight you, then sag, crying. "She said if I stopped, I'd get fat," they whisper. You sit on the curb with them until their breathing slows, and you tell them there is nothing wrong with their body. You mean it. They believe you a little.
success.art: A teenager sitting on a curb at dawn with an arm around a crying younger teen in a magenta sweatband, joggers streaming past in the background

failure.text: The column closes around them like a school of fish. Mrs. Haskins turns the boombox up. By the time you get your breath back, they're three blocks gone.
failure.art: A column of joggers swallowing a young teen like a school of fish, a woman cranking a boombox, a teenager left bent over and panting

choices.label: Set up a table of water cups and orange slices

success.text: Runners pound past. Then one stops, for an orange slice. Then another. A body that's being cared for is hard to command. Mrs. Haskins herself slows down, takes a paper cup, and starts to cry, and you hand her another slice and don't say anything at all.
success.art: A folding card table with paper cups and orange slices on a dawn sidewalk, joggers pausing to drink, a woman with a boombox at her feet crying gratefully

failure.text: Nobody stops. Cups go flying. Mrs. Haskins jogs past without breaking stride and calls out, "Water weight, sweetie!" The table folds up on your foot.
failure.art: Paper cups flying off a toppled card table as joggers stampede past, orange slices scattered across a lawn, a teenager hopping on one foot

signature.title: Operators Are Standing By
signature.text: You come downstairs for water and find your aunt at the kitchen table in her robe, phone pressed to her ear, credit card in her hand, eyes fixed on the little TV on the counter. On screen, Vonda Velour is selling the Burn Belt in three easy payments. "Call now, Burners! Operators are standing by!" Behind her, a bank of operators in magenta sweatbands answers ringing phones, and one of them has your aunt's face. The TV screen is breathing, in and out, slow and warm, like a sleeping animal.
signature.art: A dark 1980s kitchen at three in the morning, a middle-aged woman in a bathrobe at the table clutching a yellow phone receiver and a credit card, staring at a small countertop television whose screen bulges outward and glows magenta, on screen a glossy aerobics star with teased blond hair and a headset mic beside a row of telephone operators in magenta sweatbands, a teenager in pajamas on the stairs behind her, magenta glow, medium shot

choices.label: Take the phone from her gently and ask what she loves about herself

success.text: You set the receiver back in its cradle and sit down with her. It takes a minute for her eyes to clear. "My legs," she says at last, surprising herself. "I won a jitterbug contest at the Rialto in 1961 with these legs." She laughs, and on the counter the TV stops breathing, like it just lost a customer.
success.art: A teenager and their laughing aunt in a bathrobe sitting together at a kitchen table at night, a phone back on its cradle, a small television on the counter flattening into quiet static

failure.text: She clutches the phone like a lifeline. "Just three easy payments, sweetie," she says, in a voice that isn't quite hers. The operator on the line reads back her address, then yours, then every address on Crystal Street, and in the morning there is a Burn Belt on every doorstep.
failure.art: A row of suburban doorsteps at dawn each holding an identical shiny magenta exercise belt box, a tired teenager standing on their porch staring down the street at them

choices.label: Grab the upstairs extension and flood the order line with fake calls

success.text: You dial the 1-800 number and order nine thousand Burn Belts to a post office box in Antarctica. Then again. Then you call KGLM, and Mix reads the number on air with a dare attached, and half the insomniacs in Glimmer Falls start prank-ordering. The operators on screen drown in ringing phones. Vonda's smile glitches, and the signal collapses into color bars.
success.alone: You dial the 1-800 number and order nine thousand Burn Belts to a post office box in Antarctica. Then again. Then you call the KGLM request line, get yourself put on the air, and read the number out with a dare attached, and half the insomniacs in Glimmer Falls start prank-ordering. The operators on screen drown in ringing phones. Vonda's smile glitches, and the signal collapses into color bars.
success.art: A grinning teenager on a bedroom phone extension dialing furiously, a small television showing frantic sweatbanded operators buried in ringing phones, an aerobics star glitching into rainbow color bars

failure.text: The line picks up on the first ring, and Vonda herself answers. "Oh, a new Burner! Let's start with a weigh-in!" You can't hang up. You spend the rest of the night on the upstairs extension doing phone-cord lunges while she counts.
failure.art: An exhausted teenager doing lunges in a dark upstairs hallway with a phone receiver pinned to their shoulder, the curly cord stretched taut, a magenta glow spilling up the stairs

choices.label: Put both hands on the bulging screen and shove it back

success.text: The screen swells toward you like a balloon about to pop, warm and rubbery and humming. You plant your feet and push. It pushes back, then gives with a squeak like a gym shoe on hardwood, and the picture shrinks to a tiny glowing dot in the middle of the glass. Your aunt blinks, sets down the phone and says, "Why am I awake?"
success.art: A teenager bracing both hands against a television screen that bulges outward like a warm rubber balloon, magenta light pulsing around their fingers, a drowsy woman in a bathrobe blinking at the kitchen table

failure.text: Your hands sink into the screen up to the wrists. It's warm and spongy, like a gym mat, and Vonda's voice is right inside your ears: "Crunches, sweetie! Let's go!" You come to on the kitchen linoleum at dawn, mid sit-up, abs on fire, your aunt asleep at the table.
failure.art: A teenager doing sit-ups on kitchen linoleum at dawn, wrists glowing faint magenta, a woman asleep at the table with her head on her arms, a small television on the counter softly breathing

signature.title: Fitness Test Day
signature.text: The gym doors bang open as you pass the high school, and inside, under the caged lights, is the worst day of everyone's life: fitness test day. Kids in gym uniforms from every decade since 1959 are climbing ropes, straining at the pull-up bar and reaching for the sit-and-reach box, sweating and terrified. Vonda Velour paces among them with a clipboard and a whistle. "Fail and you're a before, forever!" she sings. Gracie Ochoa, a freshman from your bus stop, is dangling halfway up the rope, crying, and she can't let go.
signature.art: A high school gym at midnight under caged lights, pale students in gym uniforms from three decades climbing ropes, straining on a pull-up bar and reaching over a sit-and-reach box, a glossy aerobics star with enormous teased blond hair, a magenta leotard and teal leg warmers pacing among them with a clipboard and a whistle, a crying freshman girl clinging halfway up a rope, a teenager at the base of the rope looking up, harsh white light, wide shot

choices.label: Climb the rope and talk Gracie down

success.text: You go up hand over hand until your arms scream, hook Gracie's belt and talk her down one inch at a time. Your feet hit the mat together. The whole gym stops. Vonda raises her clipboard to write down your time, and you snatch it out of her hands and fling it into the bleachers. "She came down safe," you say. "That's the score."
success.art: A teenager and a freshman girl landing together on a blue gym mat at the foot of a climbing rope, a clipboard spinning through the air toward the bleachers, a stunned aerobics star with an open mouth

failure.text: You make it four feet up and freeze, rope burning your palms, while the whistle shrieks in time with your heartbeat. "Oh, honey," Vonda says. "We'll mark you incomplete." You hang there beside Gracie until the caged lights flicker out at dawn and you both drop onto the mat, sore and giggling with relief.
failure.art: Two teenagers dangling from climbing ropes in a dim high school gym, an aerobics star blowing a whistle below with a clipboard, caged lights flickering

choices.label: Sit down in the middle of the gym floor and refuse to be measured

success.text: You sit cross-legged on the center line and fold your arms. The whistle shrieks. You stay put. Coach Pruitt sits down beside you like she has waited twenty years for someone to start this. Then a girl in a 1962 gym suit lets go of the pull-up bar and sits too, and a boy in 1975 tube socks leaves the sit-and-reach box. Soon the whole gym is sitting and breathing, and Vonda is pacing around a floor full of people who will not be graded.
success.art: A crowd of students in gym uniforms from many decades sitting cross-legged on a gym floor around a teenager and a big fierce softball coach, an aerobics star in magenta pacing around them with a clipboard

failure.text: You sit down. Vonda leans over you, all teeth and hairspray. "Look at that," she coos, loud enough for the whole gym. "Quitters always sit first." Everyone keeps climbing and straining around you, and you sit alone on the cold floor with your face burning until the lights go out.
failure.art: An aerobics star with huge teased hair leaning over a teenager sitting alone on a gym floor, students in gym uniforms climbing ropes and straining on bars all around them

choices.label: Swipe the clipboard and change every score to PRESENT

success.text: You slide in behind her during a whistle blast, palm the clipboard and go to work with your pencil eraser. Every number, every red check, every FAIL becomes PRESENT. When Vonda reads the scores aloud, kids from every decade hear their names and one word, present, and one by one they drop off the ropes and bars and walk out into the night, still in their uniforms, lighter.
success.art: A sneaky teenager crouched behind the bleachers furiously erasing a clipboard, students in old gym uniforms from many decades letting go of ropes and walking out open gym doors into the night

failure.text: She catches your wrist without looking. "Cheating, sweetie? That's ten laps." You run them. Then ten more. The gym floor stretches with every lap, the far wall drifting away, and you are still running when the sun comes up and the janitor finds you jogging in place by the bleachers.
failure.art: An exhausted teenager jogging laps around an impossibly long stretched gym floor at sunrise, an aerobics star with a whistle and clipboard watching, a puzzled janitor with a mop by the bleachers

signature.title: Your After Picture
signature.place: The Glitter Box dressing room, after the late show
signature.text: The Glitter Box dressing room has cleared out after the late show, leaving a long counter of wigs and greasepaint under a row of bulb-ringed mirrors. You sit down to wipe off your Halloween face paint, and your reflection does not wipe along with you. It is smiling. It is glossy, airbrushed and perfectly toned, in a magenta sweatband and leotard: the you Vonda's tape says you are supposed to be. It leans out of the glass and offers you its hand. "Don't you want to be your after picture?" it asks, in Vonda's voice. "I'll take it from here."
signature.art: A small theater dressing room after the late show, a long counter of wigs on foam heads and greasepaint tins under a row of bulb-ringed mirrors, a teenager in smeared Halloween face paint sitting in front of one mirror holding a tissue, and their reflection, glossy and airbrushed in a magenta sweatband and leotard, leaning out of the glass with a hand held out toward them, warm bulb light and magenta glow from the mirror, medium shot

choices.label: Tell your After everything your body already does right

success.text: "My body carries my crew home," you tell it. "It dances badly and hugs hard and runs from monsters every single night this week. It isn't a before. It's the whole movie." Your After's smile flickers. Its gloss smears like wet paint, and it slides back into the glass, just your ordinary reflection again, face paint on its chin, looking proud of you.
success.art: A teenager with smeared face paint speaking firmly to a bulb-ringed mirror, their glossy airbrushed reflection smearing like wet paint and melting back into an ordinary proud reflection of themselves

failure.text: You open your mouth and what comes out is Vonda's voice, listing your flaws. Your After nods along sweetly. You stagger away from the mirror an hour later remembering every mean thing anyone ever said about your body, and the reflection in the bus window home keeps smiling the wrong smile.
failure.art: A downcast teenager riding a night bus staring at the window, their reflection in the glass smiling a glossy airbrushed smile in a magenta sweatband, streetlights streaking past

choices.label: Challenge your After to a vogue-off it can't count its way through

success.text: Glory sweeps in from the wings, takes one look and calls the category: "Realness, honey, and the realness is you." You hit a dip, a duckwalk and hand choreography so committed it counts as a sport. Your After can only do Vonda's count, five, six, seven, eight, and it cannot follow a single beat it wasn't programmed for. It stammers, glitches and folds back into the mirror like a tape rewinding.
success.alone: You sweep in from the wings and call the category yourself: "Realness, honey, and the realness is me." You hit a dip, a duckwalk and hand choreography so committed it counts as a sport. Your After can only do Vonda's count, five, six, seven, eight, and it cannot follow a single beat it wasn't programmed for. It stammers, glitches and folds back into the mirror like a tape rewinding.
success.art: A teenager striking a dramatic vogue dip in a theatre dressing room while a drag queen in sequins judges with a fan, a glossy reflection in a magenta sweatband glitching and folding back into a bulb-ringed mirror

failure.text: Your After matches you move for move, crisp and perfect, until you stumble and it doesn't. "See?" it says, sympathetic. "Isn't it easier to just be me?" Every mirror on the counter shows your After now, smiling, and you have to leave the dressing room walking backward.
failure.art: A row of bulb-ringed dressing room mirrors each showing the same glossy smiling reflection in a magenta sweatband, a stumbling teenager backing away toward the door

choices.label: Grab its glossy wrist and shove it back into the glass

success.text: You catch its wrist and shove. It's strong, but it has never had to work for anything, and you have been running from nightmares all week. It slips back into the mirror with a wet pop like a bubble of hair gel, and you hang a feather boa over the glass for good measure.
success.art: A teenager shoving a glossy airbrushed reflection back into a bulb-ringed mirror by the wrist, a pink feather boa draped ready on the counter among wigs and greasepaint

failure.text: It grabs you back, and for one dizzy second you are on the other side of the glass, inside a gold-flecked aerobics studio, while your After sits at the counter in your clothes, smiling. You claw your way out through the bulbs, but the burn in your thighs lasts all night.
failure.art: A teenager trapped inside a gold-flecked aerobics studio seen through a bulb-ringed mirror, pressing hands to the glass, their glossy smiling double seated at the dressing room counter wearing their clothes

signature.title: No Cool-Down
signature.text: Studio A is packed wall to wall with Burners. The mirror wall has become one giant screen, and Vonda, ten feet tall, leads them through the final tape, BURN IT ALL OFF!, every rep faster than the last. People drop to the floor and get back up. A digital scale in the corner flashes numbers that never stop changing. The room is so hot the mirrors are fogging. "Nobody leaves," Vonda sings, "until there's nothing left of you."
signature.art: A sweltering aerobics studio at midnight packed wall to wall with people in sweatbands, the mirror wall turned into one huge screen showing a ten-foot glossy aerobics star with teased blond hair, a magenta leotard and a headset mic leading the class, exhausted people dropping to the floor and pushing back up, a digital bathroom scale flashing red numbers in the corner, fogged mirrors, a teenager pushing through the crowd, hot magenta light and steam, wide shot

choices.label: Smash the scale in the corner

success.text: CRACK. The numbers die mid-flash. The beat stutters. Half the room stops and looks down at themselves like they've just remembered they have bodies, and that those bodies are tired, and that's allowed.
success.art: A teenager swinging a bat into a sparking digital scale in an aerobics studio, the numbers shattering, people stopping mid-exercise and looking at themselves

failure.text: The scale flashes one word across every mirror in the room: BEFORE. Every Burner turns to look at you. "Oh, honey," says Vonda, so sweetly that it stings for a week.
failure.art: A mirror wall flashing a single cruel word in neon pink, a room full of sweatbanded people turning to stare at a frozen teenager holding a bat

choices.label: Sneak into the sound booth and swap in a cool-down tape

success.text: In the booth you swap cassettes: slow jams, Sade, Cyndi singing "Time After Time." Bodies slow. People stretch. People breathe. People sit down on the floor and hold hands with strangers. On the mirror, Vonda glitches into slow motion, confused, her smile sagging at the corners.
success.art: An aerobics studio softening into a gentle cool-down, people stretching and sitting together on the floor, a glitching aerobics star moving in slow motion on the mirror screen, a teen in the sound booth window

failure.text: The tape won't eject. The booth door locks behind you. You watch through the glass, pounding, as the class goes faster, and faster, and faster.
failure.art: A teenager pounding on the glass of a locked sound booth while a frenzied aerobics class speeds up into a blur beyond it

signature.title: Slumber Party Workout
signature.place: Ronnie Patterson's slumber party, the rec room, 1 a.m.
signature.text: At Ronnie Patterson's slumber party somebody digs BURN IT OFF! out of her mom's tape drawer and puts it on as a joke, and for ten minutes everyone is shrieking at the leotards. Then the laughing stops. Everyone else in a sleeping bag is doing crunches in perfect unison, eyes glassy, counting along with Vonda. Ronnie pinches her own stomach and says, in a voice that sounds dubbed, "Nobody loves a before picture." The pizza in the box has gone cold and untouched. Vonda smiles out of the screen. "Who's next, sweeties?"
signature.art: A cozy wood-paneled 1980s rec room at one in the morning, girls in sleeping bags doing crunches in perfect unison with glassy eyes, a teenage girl in a nightshirt pinching her own stomach, a boxy television glowing with a smiling aerobics star in a magenta leotard and teal leg warmers, a cold untouched pizza box on the shag carpet, a teenager holding a pillow, magenta TV glow and a dim lamp, wide shot

choices.label: Bop the nearest crunching kid with a pillow and start an all-out pillow fight

success.text: Whump. A pillow to the back of Ronnie's head breaks her count. She blinks, grabs a pillow and whumps you back, and in seconds the rec room is a blizzard of feathers and shrieking. Nobody can do crunches in a pillow fight. On the screen Vonda counts to eight, then to eight again, then stammers, her smile slipping, while the whole party collapses in a giggling heap and finally eats the pizza.
success.art: A wild slumber party pillow fight in a 1980s rec room at night, feathers swirling, kids in pajamas shrieking with laughter, a flustered aerobics star stammering on the glowing television

failure.text: You swing, the pillow bursts, and Vonda laughs along from the screen. "Ooh, a cardio burst! Feathers count as reps!" Everyone keeps crunching in a snowfall of feathers, and somehow you are crunching too, sneezing, until the tape runs out at dawn.
failure.art: Kids in sleeping bags doing crunches in a snowfall of feathers in a dark rec room, a burst pillow on the carpet, a grinning aerobics star in a magenta leotard counting on the television

choices.label: Hit REC and record the late-night monster movie right over her

success.text: You flip to Channel 44's Creature Double Feature and punch REC. Vonda's face smears sideways mid-count and turns into a giant rubber ant stomping a cardboard city. The crunching stops. Everyone blinks at the screen. "Wait," says Ronnie, "is that the ant one? I love the ant one." The whole party piles onto the couch with the cold pizza.
success.art: Kids in pajamas piled on a couch with cold pizza watching a giant rubber ant stomp a cardboard city on a glowing television, a teenager holding a VCR remote triumphantly

failure.text: The record tab is snapped off. Of course it is. The VCR whirs, spits the tape onto the carpet, swallows it again, and Vonda comes back mid-sentence: "Sneaky, sneaky! That's twenty extra burpees for the whole slumber party." Nobody sleeps.
failure.art: A VCR spitting a tangled videotape onto shag carpet in a dark rec room, a smiling aerobics star on the television wagging her finger, groaning kids in sleeping bags doing burpees

choices.label: Turn the TV to face the wall and start a circle: one thing you love about the person on your left

success.text: You heave the TV around to face the wall, sit down among the sleeping bags and say, "Okay. Circle. One thing you love about the person on your left." It is awkward for exactly one round. Then Ronnie says Dee has the best laugh in the eighth grade, and Dee says Ronnie's freckles look like a map of the stars, and by the end of the circle half the room is crying the good kind of crying and the TV is muttering to the wallpaper.
success.art: Kids in pajamas sitting in a circle on sleeping bags in a 1980s rec room, laughing and hugging, a television turned around to face the wall glowing faintly

failure.text: You turn the TV to the wall, but Vonda's voice keeps coming out of the speaker, and every compliment someone starts, she finishes for them: "You have such a pretty face, if only." The circle breaks up in hurt silence, and you spend the rest of the night trying to fix it.
failure.art: Kids in pajamas sitting apart in hurt silence in a dim rec room, a television turned toward the wall glowing magenta, a worried teenager in the middle of the scattered sleeping bags

signature.title: Biggest Burner
signature.place: The Glimmer Falls Community Center, a midnight weigh-in
signature.text: The town council has gone Burner. At midnight the Community Center is packed for the Biggest Burner Halloween Challenge, sponsored by BURN IT OFF!, with a giant industrial scale on the stage, clusters of magenta balloons and a gold trophy shaped like a sweatband. Vonda emcees from a TV on a rolling cart, calling contestants up one by one while the crowd applauds every number on the dial. Your gym teacher is in line. So is the mayor. And at the top of the contestant clipboard, in handwriting you don't recognize, is your name.
signature.art: A packed small-town community center at midnight, a giant industrial dial scale on the stage under clusters of magenta balloons, a gold trophy in the shape of a sweatband on a table, a glossy aerobics star with teased blond hair smiling out of a television on a rolling cart, a line of townspeople in sweatbands waiting at the stage steps including a man in a mayor's sash, a teenager at the end of the line, warm stage light and magenta balloons, wide shot from the folding chairs

choices.label: Climb on the scale with the whole crew at once and declare it a team sport

success.text: "Team weigh-in!" you yell, and your crew piles onto the scale behind you, then Mr. Delgado the gym teacher, then the mayor, laughing, then half the line, arms around each other, until the needle spins all the way around the dial and snaps off with a ping. The crowd roars. There is no number for a whole town hugging. On the TV cart, Vonda opens her mouth and only static comes out.
success.art: A teenager, friends, a gym teacher and a laughing mayor all piled onto a giant industrial scale on a community center stage, the needle snapped off, a television on a cart crackling with static, a cheering crowd

failure.text: Your crew piles on, but the scale only counts you. The needle swings, the TV dings like a game show, and Vonda coos, "Ooh, honey, let's talk about that number!" Your face burns. You walk off the stage and out of the building, and it takes a long, long walk home to shake her voice out of your ears.
failure.art: A red-faced teenager walking off a community center stage past a giant industrial scale, a glossy aerobics star leaning toward them from a television on a rolling cart, a crowd watching

choices.label: Crawl under the stage and unplug Vonda's TV cart

success.text: You slither under the stage through decades of stacked chairs and dust bunnies and find the extension cord. One yank. Vonda blinks out mid-coo, and the line of contestants mumbles and shuffles and starts asking each other what time it is and why they are holding their shoes. Somebody finds the lights. Somebody else finds the doughnuts.
success.art: A dusty crawlspace under a community center stage, a teenager yanking an extension cord, above them a confused crowd in sweatbands blinking under dimming lights

failure.text: You yank the wrong cord and the stage lights die instead. Vonda's TV glows brighter in the dark, the only light in the hall, and the crowd presses toward it, chanting your name to come up next. You crawl out the back under the stage and run for it.
failure.art: A dark community center lit only by a glowing television on a cart showing a smiling aerobics star, townspeople in sweatbands crowding toward it, a teenager crawling out from under the stage

choices.label: Take the mic and ask the room to cheer for something their bodies did this week

success.text: You take the mic. "Forget the dial. Tell me something your body did this week." Silence. Then the mayor says, "I carried my granddaughter up three flights of stairs." Mr. Delgado: "I danced at my sister's wedding." A little kid: "I did a cartwheel!" Every answer gets louder applause than any number did. The giant scale creaks, forgotten, and the gold trophy tips over on its own.
success.art: A teenager at a microphone on a community center stage, townspeople in sweatbands raising their hands and smiling, a little kid mid-cartwheel in the aisle, a gold trophy tipping over beside a giant scale

failure.text: You take the mic and your voice cracks into feedback. Vonda's TV cart rolls itself across the stage until it is right beside you, and she pats the inside of the screen sympathetically. "Stage fright burns calories, sweetie!" The crowd laughs. You hand back the mic and sit down.
failure.art: A teenager wincing at a squealing microphone on a community center stage, a television on a rolling cart beside them showing a sympathetic aerobics star, a laughing crowd

signature.title: Dance Till You Drop
signature.place: The KGLM Halloween Dance-a-Thon, Starlight Mall center court, October 30
signature.text: The KGLM Halloween Dance-a-Thon was supposed to raise money for the children's hospital. Thirty hours in, it has raised Vonda. She fills every TV in the electronics store display, her count booming over the mall speakers, and the couples on the center court floor cannot stop moving, sagging against each other, sneakers squeaking, eyes glassy. Every hour a buzzer sounds and Vonda calls out the couple she likes least, "Too slow, sweeties! Out!", and their own feet march them toward the glowing screens. Sunny Castellanos is out on the floor in her racing chair, refusing to be counted out, but her partner is about to fall.
signature.art: A 1980s mall center court at night during a dance marathon, exhausted couples sagging against each other on a parquet floor with sneakers squeaking, a wall of televisions in an electronics store window all showing a glossy aerobics star counting with her fingers, a 22-year-old woman with dark curls and an orange headband dancing fiercely in her neon-orange racing wheelchair, her partner about to fall, a teenager running onto the floor, mixed neon light, wide shot

choices.label: Drag folding chairs onto the floor and call a sit-down dance, with Sunny leading

success.text: You haul a stack of folding chairs onto the floor and shout, "Sit-down dance! Sunny's leading!" Sunny grins and spins into the center, all shoulders and arms and attitude, and couple by couple the exhausted dancers drop into chairs and follow her: shoulder rolls, hand jive, the swim. It is the best dancing the marathon has seen in thirty hours. Vonda calls out couple after couple, but you cannot eliminate somebody who is resting and having the time of their life.
success.art: A young woman in a racing wheelchair leading a joyful seated dance in a mall center court at night, rows of tired dancers in folding chairs doing the hand jive, a teenager clapping beside her

failure.text: You haul in the chairs, but Vonda's count is faster than your voice, and the couples will not sit, too afraid of the buzzer. Sunny keeps dancing in the center with fierce, furious style while everyone else staggers on around her, and you finish the night as her partner, worn to the bone.
failure.art: A young woman in a racing wheelchair dancing fiercely in a mall center court at night while exhausted couples stagger around her, a worn-out teenager as her partner, televisions glowing magenta

choices.label: Get into the electronics store and hit PAUSE on every VCR in the display

success.text: Toby knows every VCR in the electronics store by model number. The two of you sprint down the display hitting PAUSE, PAUSE, PAUSE, and Vonda freezes mid-kick on every screen in a jittering, flickering row, one leg up, mouth open on "eight." The count stops. Out on the center court, two hundred dancers stop with it and sink to the floor, wheezing and laughing and pulling off their shoes.
success.alone: You don't know a single VCR by model number, so you sprint down the display slapping every button marked PAUSE, PAUSE, PAUSE, and Vonda freezes mid-kick on every screen in a jittering, flickering row, one leg up, mouth open on "eight." The count stops. Out on the center court, two hundred dancers stop with it and sink to the floor, wheezing and laughing and pulling off their shoes.
success.art: A wall of televisions in an electronics store all frozen on an aerobics star mid-kick, two teenagers at the VCR display, exhausted dancers sinking to the floor of the mall court beyond

failure.text: You hit PAUSE and the screen unpauses itself. You hit STOP and it rewinds, and every dancer on the floor dances backward, faster and faster, sneakers screeching, while Vonda laughs in reverse. The store's security gate rolls down with you inside, and you watch the rest of the marathon through the bars.
failure.art: A teenager gripping the bars of a rolled-down security gate in a mall electronics store at night, televisions rewinding, dancers spinning backward on the center court floor

choices.label: Wade onto the floor and help the fallen dancers off it, one by one

success.text: Whenever someone starts to fall, you are there, hauling them off the floor with an arm under their shoulders. Someone sees you and does the same, then the cheerleaders from the bleachers, then the mall cops, until every exhausted couple has been helped off the court to sit on the fountain's edge with a paper cup of water. Vonda calls the next couple out, and there is not a single dancer left on the floor to call.
success.art: A teenager helping an exhausted dancer off a mall center court floor at night, cheerleaders and mall security doing the same, tired couples resting on a fountain edge with paper cups

failure.text: You catch the first dancer, but the floor grabs your own sneakers the moment you step onto it, and suddenly you are in the marathon too, partnered with a sleepwalking assistant manager from the shoe store. You dance until dawn, and your feet do not forgive you for a week.
failure.art: A teenager dancing with a sleepwalking shoe store assistant manager on a mall center court floor at dawn, both exhausted, televisions glowing magenta behind them

finale.title: The Final Burn
finale.text: On Halloween every TV on Crystal Street turns to face out its window, and every one plays Vonda. The whole town is in the street in sweatbands, working out around the Heartstone in rings, and the geode pulses magenta with every rep. Vonda steps out of the biggest screen in a shower of glitter sweat, headset mic on, smile locked. "Last set, Burners! Burn it all off! Burn until there's nothing wrong with you, because there's nothing left!"
finale.art: A suburban roundabout on Halloween night, rings of townspeople in costumes and magenta sweatbands doing frantic aerobics around a huge purple crystal geode that pulses magenta, televisions in every house window turned to face the street, a giant glossy aerobics star with enormous teased blond hair, a magenta leotard, teal leg warmers and a headset microphone stepping out of the biggest screen in a shower of glitter, four teenagers in homemade costumes facing her, magenta and cyan light, wide shot

choices.label: Tackle the master VCR and rip out the tape

success.text: You plow through three rings of Burners, hit the master deck shoulder-first and tear the tape out in a shining ribbon. Every TV on the street snaps to snow. Vonda freezes mid-kick and dissolves into tracking lines. The town collapses onto the lawns, aching and confused and free.
success.art: A teenager ripping a ribbon of videotape from a VCR as every television on a suburban street fills with static, a glittering aerobics star breaking into tracking lines, exhausted townspeople collapsing on lawns

failure.text: Vonda catches you by the collar with one glittering hand. "Look at all that energy! Let's put it to work!" You're in the front row now, doing burpees, and you can't stop.
failure.art: An aerobics star holding a teenager by the collar and setting them in the front row of a frantic outdoor workout

choices.label: Get the whole street doing the Chicken Dance instead

success.text: You flap your elbows. The crew flaps theirs. Then the Haskinses, the mailman and your science teacher. Nobody can hate their body while doing the Chicken Dance; it's scientifically impossible. The rhythm breaks, Vonda's count dissolves into clucking, and she flickers out like a TV at sign-off.
success.art: An entire suburban street in Halloween costumes doing the Chicken Dance and laughing around a glowing geode, an aerobics star flickering out like a television signing off

failure.text: They chicken dance, all right: in perfect unison, at triple speed, to her count. "Ooh, a new routine," Vonda purrs. "Again!"
failure.art: A crowd doing a frantic synchronized chicken dance at impossible speed around a glowing geode, a delighted aerobics star clapping the beat

choices.label: Play the raw tape and let Wanda speak for herself

success.text: You slam the raw tape into the master deck. Every screen on Crystal Street flickers, and there she is, the real Wanda, round and radiant and laughing: "Your body isn't a before picture, baby. It's the whole movie. Dance because it feels good." The Burners stop. Vonda stops. She looks down at her own glittering hands like she's hearing her own voice for the first time in three years. "That's me," she whispers. "That was always me." She peels off her sweatband and dances, off the count, for joy, and the whole street dances with her, slow and silly and sitting down when they want to.
success.art: Every television on a Halloween street showing a joyful, curvy dancer laughing, a glittering aerobics star pulling off her sweatband with wonder, townspeople of every shape dancing freely and sitting together on lawns around a softly glowing geode

failure.text: The deck jams and the raw tape won't seat. You have Wanda's real voice right there in your hands, but the town can't hear it over the count, not yet.
failure.art: A teenager struggling to jam a videotape into a stubborn VCR while the workout around them roars on, an aerobics star laughing overhead

choices.label: Remember the first tapes at home: hit REC on the master deck and record the street laughing over her count

success.text: The first nights of the week, when the tape crept into living rooms and kitchens, taught you the secret: Vonda is a recording, and a recording cannot keep up with real people having fun. You shove through the rings to the master deck, punch REC and hold up the microphone. Your crew starts it, then the Haskinses, then the whole street: laughing, booing, singing off-key, telling terrible jokes. The master tape records right over her count. When Vonda opens her mouth for "and burn," what comes out of every TV on Crystal Street is the town cracking up, and the Burners stop to listen, and laugh, and sit down on the lawns.
success.art: A teenager pressing a button on a big master VCR in a suburban street at night while holding up a microphone, neighbors in sweatbands laughing and sitting down on lawns, televisions in every house glowing with static

failure.text: You punch REC, but the master deck's record tab is snapped off, and it spits the microphone cord back at you. "Nice try, sweetie," Vonda sings from every screen. You stumble back into the outer ring, short of breath but still yourself.
failure.art: A teenager stumbling back from a master VCR deck into rings of neighbors in sweatbands working out around a glowing purple geode at night, a glossy aerobics star smiling from every television

choices.label: Refuse to be counted, like you did all week, and pull your neighbors out of the rings

success.text: All week Vonda tried to measure you: on the street at dawn, on a gym rope, on a stage with a dial. All week you refused. So you step out of the ring, plant yourself in the middle of Crystal Street and stop moving. Then you start pulling people out. Mrs. Haskins. Your science teacher. The kid from homeroom. One by one you take their wrists and sit them down on the curb beside you, and every person who sits makes the rings thinner and the count weaker, until Vonda is shouting reps at a street full of people who have decided they are done. Her voice cracks, and every TV goes to snow.
success.art: A teenager sitting firmly on a suburban curb at night, pulling a neighbor in a sweatband down to sit beside them, a growing row of seated townspeople, rings of exercisers thinning around a glowing purple geode, televisions fizzing

failure.text: You plant your feet, but the count drags at your knees like a current, and the people you pull out keep drifting back in. You end up on the curb alone, stubborn and out of breath, but you are sitting, and she cannot make you stand.
failure.art: A stubborn out-of-breath teenager sitting alone on a curb at night, rings of neighbors in magenta sweatbands still working out around a glowing purple geode, a glittering aerobics star smiling on a big screen

choices.label: Say what you learned the night before Halloween: a body isn't a before, it's the whole movie

success.text: The night before Halloween you learned to say it out loud: a body is not a before picture, it is the whole movie. You say it now, straight to Vonda, and then you slam the raw tape into the master deck. Every screen flickers, and there is Wanda, round and radiant and laughing, saying the very same thing in her own voice. Vonda stops mid-kick and looks down at her glittering hands. "That's me," she whispers. "That was always me." She pulls off her sweatband and dances, off the count, for joy, and Crystal Street dances with her, slow and silly, sitting down whenever anyone wants to.
success.art: A glittering aerobics star pulling off her magenta sweatband and dancing joyfully off the beat around a softly glowing purple geode at night, neighbors dancing slow and silly beside her or resting on the grass, a teenager beaming

failure.text: You say it, and you mean it, but the count is still booming and the raw tape skips in the deck. Vonda hesitates, one glittering hand at her ear as if she heard something familiar, and then the beat swallows it.
failure.art: A glittering aerobics star pausing mid-kick with one hand at her ear beside a pulsing purple geode at night, rings of neighbors still exercising, a teenager beside a jammed master VCR

best.title: The Whole Movie
best.text: On November first the Burners hang their sweatbands on the Heartstone like retired jerseys. Coach Pruitt gets the district memo torn up at a school board meeting she will describe for years. Toby cuts the raw footage into DANCE FOR EVERY BODY WITH WANDA, and Rewind Video replaces every copy of the old tape for free. In December, Wanda Fenn drives down from Sacramento to teach a free Saturday class at the Glitter Box, with Sunny co-leading from her chair. Mrs. Haskins comes and dances in the back row. Nobody counts anything except, badly, to eight.
best.art: A joyful Saturday dance class on a small theater stage, a curvy woman in her forties in a purple tracksuit leading with her arms flung wide, a young woman with dark curls in a neon-orange racing wheelchair co-leading beside her, people of every age, size and body dancing and laughing, a middle-aged woman dancing in the back row, magenta sweatbands hanging on a purple crystal rock outside the window, warm bright stage light, wide shot

good.title: Tracking Error
good.text: The tapes demagnetize all over town and the joggers stop running. Nobody ever really says why. Life goes back to normal, mostly. But you still hear that perky count in the back of your head sometimes, when you reach for dessert, and every time, you tell it to shut up, and you take the bigger piece.
good.art: A teenager at a suburban kitchen table grinning as they lift a big slice of chocolate cake onto a plate, and in the background a dark switched-off television with the faint reflection of a blond aerobics star scowling in the glass, warm kitchen light, medium shot

bittersweet.title: Rewind
bittersweet.text: You survive the week. Mrs. Haskins spends three days in the hospital with exhaustion and recovers. The kid from your homeroom transfers schools at Christmas. And in the spring a brand-new workout tape hits the shelves at Rewind Video, with a new name and a new smiling face on the box, and the very same voice.
bittersweet.art: A video rental store new-release shelf with a fresh row of workout tapes, the boxes showing a new smiling woman in a turquoise leotard, a faint pink glow along their edges, a teenager in a jacket standing in the aisle staring at them uneasily, fluorescent store light, medium shot

bad.title: Feel the Burn
bad.text: You're in the tape now. Back row, gold-flecked studio, magenta sweatband, doing jumping jacks forever. When your crew rents BURN IT OFF! from Rewind Video to look for clues, they see you behind Vonda's shoulder, smiling, waving, counting, and you cannot hear them screaming your name.
bad.art: A boxy television in a dark living room playing an aerobics video in a gold-flecked studio, a glossy blond aerobics star kicking at the front and a teenager in a magenta sweatband in the back row smiling blankly and waving, three friends on the couch in front of the set leaning toward the screen with frightened faces, magenta TV glow, medium wide shot from behind the couch
